messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: SEV=1 pager triggered — GPU OOM spike during prefill on cluster-preempt-prod-3. Multiple container restarts observed. Paging @Amir (oncall). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom
Amir: Ack — I'm on it. Jumping into logs and infra console now.
Jess: Seen the alerts. Quick log snippet from runtime:
```
[2026-03-18T02:12:43Z] runtime.prefill v3 pid=1245 gpu0 OOM allocate 6.2GB
error: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY -> container SIGKILL, restart loop
[2026-03-18T02:14:11Z] runtime.prefill pid=1301 gpu0 illegal instruction (possibly corrupted kernel after oom)
```
Jess: Pattern = long-context prefills (>32k tokens) + bursty fanout -> kvcache blowup and OOM.
Kelly: Support report: multiple customers saw 5xx for streaming generation ~02:10-02:40 UTC. Ticket #CS-4129 from RedwoodHealth (high-touch) — they saw mid-stream disconnects.
Lina: Notified RedwoodHealth via PM. They're monitoring — want ETA for mitigation.
Amir: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Hotpatch prefill token cap to 512 for cluster-preempt-prod-3, 2) Reduce PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY 4->1, 3) Route new requests to cold-model fallback for same route, 4) Cordon affected nodes and drain remaining long-prefill containers. Will run canary first.
Tony: I have a small config patch ready: set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=512 and PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 in /etc/redwood/runtime/prefill.conf. Also a quick kvcache trim hook: trim_kvcache_on_prefill=true when tokens>1024.
Jess: Recommend enabling kvcache trimming as well — should prevent runaway memory growth mid-prefill.
Amir: Applying canary to 2 nodes in prefill-hotpool now. Will watch OOM count and container restarts.
IncidentBot: Deploy started: config-update prefill-hotpatch -> canary nodes (2/50). CI:green.
Amir: Canary looks stable for 3m. No new restarts on canary nodes. Proceeding to 20% rollout.
IncidentBot: Deploy update: canary -> 20% nodes.
Kelly: Customer errors dropping — RedwoodHealth reports no further disconnects after ~02:30 UTC. Other affected customers reporting improvements.
Jess: We're still seeing a tail of restarts on older nodes; scheduling node cordon + drain for 5 nodes with most restarts. Routing rule applied so new requests land on patched pool or cold fallback.
Tony: Kvcache trim flag rolled out with canary. Observed kvcache size reduce ~60% for long sessions on patched nodes.
Amir: All mitigations in place. Restart rate back to baseline. I’ll keep pager open for 30m to ensure stability.
Lina: Confirmed RedwoodHealth notified and accepted temporary mitigation. They requested postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.
Jess: Next steps: 1) telemetry alert tuning (raise prefill token alarm threshold + add kvcache growth alert), 2) implement long-prefill backpressure (reject >16k tokens at API layer), 3) postmortem with root cause (kvcache growth + prefetch concurrency interaction).
Amir: Creating incident ticket INC-2026-0318 and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem. Oncall handoff scheduled: I'm handing to Jess at 08:00 UTC.
Amir: Closing pager — mitigation successful, customers stable. Will follow up with a short postmortem and action items. :thumbsup:
Jess: Thx — will own the PM and next-day followup.
IncidentBot: Pager closed by Amir. Duration: ~52 minutes.
